subject: Trading
title: How Crashes Spread
description: A quick, practical guide to How Crashes Spread.

hook.text: Thailand's currency collapsed in 1997. Within months, Indonesia, South Korea, and Russia were in crisis too.

buildup.text: Financial contagion spreads through trade links, shared creditors, and—most powerfully—investor panic.

discovery.text: When investors lose money in one market, they sell assets in other markets to raise cash, spreading the crisis.

twist.text: Contagion often spreads to countries with strong fundamentals. Guilt by geography or asset class is enough.

climax.text: In a globalized world, no market is an island. A crisis anywhere can become a crisis everywhere.

punchline.text: In connected markets, one fire can burn down the whole neighborhood.

quiz.question: How does financial contagion spread?
options: Through trade links, shared creditors, and investor panic
